cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant (~570 CE) to Aminah bint Wahb; his father Abdullah had passed away before his birth.
The leading tribe of Makkah and custodians of the Ka'bah; the Prophet ﷺ was from its Banu Hashim clan.
Before Islam, around 360 idols stood in and around the Ka'bah; they were destroyed at the Conquest of Makkah.
A pre-Islamic practice of seeking decisions through marked arrows, forbidden in the Qur'an (5:3).
The cave on Jabal an-Nur where the Prophet ﷺ used to retreat, and where Jibril (AS) brought the first revelation.
At the Prophet's ﷺ birth, his mother saw a light by which the palaces of Syria (Busra) became visible — a sign of his coming.
Narrations mention idols toppling and other extraordinary signs occurring at the time of the Prophet's ﷺ birth.
The well that sprang up for Hajar and the infant Isma'il (AS) in Makkah; its water still flows today.
The two hills between which Hajar ran seeking water for Isma'il (AS); pilgrims re-enact this in Sa'ee.
Ibrahim (AS) was commanded in a dream to sacrifice his son; Allah ransomed him with a ram — commemorated at Eid al-Adha.
The stone from Paradise set in the eastern corner of the Ka'bah; the Prophet ﷺ resolved a tribal dispute over placing it.
The stone on which Ibrahim (AS) stood while building the Ka'bah, bearing the marks of his feet.
Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) raised the foundations of the Ka'bah, the first house of worship established for mankind.
Abraha's army marched with elephants to destroy the Ka'bah and was destroyed by birds sent by Allah — the year of the Prophet's ﷺ birth.
The flocks of birds Allah sent against Abraha's army, pelting them with stones of baked clay (Sura Fil).
'Read!' — the first word of revelation, brought by Jibril (AS) to the Prophet ﷺ in the Cave of Hira.
A Christian monk who recognised signs of prophethood in the young Muhammad ﷺ during a trade journey and warned Abu Talib to protect him.
The city where the Prophet ﷺ was rejected and pelted with stones; he refused to have its people destroyed, hoping their children would believe.
The Prophet ﷺ tended sheep in his youth, saying every prophet had done the same.
'The Trustworthy' — the title Makkans gave the Prophet ﷺ for his honesty even before prophethood.
At 25, the Prophet ﷺ married Khadijah (RA), a noble businesswoman; she was the first to believe in him.
A pact of Makkan chiefs to defend the oppressed; the Prophet ﷺ witnessed it as a youth and praised it even after Islam.
Early Muslims fled persecution to the just Christian king Negus of Abyssinia, who protected them after hearing Sura Maryam.
Quraysh boycotted the Prophet's ﷺ clan for about three years; the boycott document was later found eaten by termites except Allah's name.
The year the Prophet ﷺ lost both his wife Khadijah (RA) and his uncle and protector Abu Talib.
The miraculous night journey to Jerusalem and ascension through the heavens, where the five daily prayers were prescribed.
The heavenly mount that carried the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah to Jerusalem on the night journey.
A miracle in which the moon appeared split in two at the Prophet's ﷺ gesture (Sura Qamar 54:1).
Pledges by the people of Yathrib (Madinah) to support and protect the Prophet ﷺ, paving the way for the Hijrah.
The Prophet's ﷺ migration from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE, from which the Islamic calendar begins.
The cave where the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) hid during the Hijrah; a spider's web and dove's nest concealed the entrance.
The first mosque of Islam, built on arrival at the outskirts of Madinah; praying there carries the reward of an umrah.
The first major battle (2 AH), where 313 Muslims defeated a much larger Quraysh army with the help of angels.
The battle (3 AH) where archers leaving their post turned near-victory into hardship; Hamza (RA) was martyred.
The siege of Madinah (5 AH) repelled by digging a trench, suggested by Salman al-Farsi (RA).
A ten-year truce with Quraysh that the Qur'an called a clear victory; it opened the way for Islam to spread.
The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah with 10,000 companions, forgave its people, and cleansed the Ka'bah of idols.

clues: No superiority of Arab over non-Arab
cards.info: The Prophet's ﷺ final sermon at his only hajj, proclaiming human equality, sanctity of life and property, and completion of the religion.
The mosque built by the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, where he is buried; one prayer there equals a thousand elsewhere.
Poor companions who lived on a shaded platform of Masjid Nabawi, devoting themselves to learning from the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ spent his infancy with her tribe in the desert; her household filled with blessing while he was in her care.
As a child among Banu Sa'd, two angels opened his chest and washed his heart with Zamzam water.

clues: On the way back from Madinah
cards.info: His mother died at Abwa returning from a visit to her relatives, leaving him an orphan with neither parent.
After Aminah's death his grandfather raised him and would seat him on his own place beside the Ka'bah.
When Quraysh argued over who would set the Black Stone, he ﷺ laid it on a cloak and had every clan carry a corner together.
His words to Khadijah (RA) after the first revelation, as he returned from Hira.
He recognised the revelation as the same Namus sent to Musa (AS), and wished he would live to support him.
The house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, where the early Muslims met and learned in secret for about three years.
Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA) was the first person killed for the faith, refusing to renounce it under torture.
Bilal (RA) was pinned beneath a boulder in the desert heat, repeating 'One, One' until Abu Bakr bought and freed him.
He embraced Islam in anger at Abu Jahl's abuse of his nephew, and became a shield for the Muslims.

clues: Set out with a drawn sword
cards.info: On his way to kill the Prophet ﷺ he heard Sura Taha being recited in his sister's house and accepted Islam that day.
The just Christian king who sheltered the Muslim emigrants and refused to hand them back to Quraysh.
At Ta'if the angel offered to destroy the town between the two mountains; he ﷺ asked instead that their descendants be believers.

clues: A slave with a tray of grapes
cards.info: The Christian servant who brought grapes after Ta'if and accepted him on hearing him mention Yunus (AS).

clues: His horse sank in the sand
cards.info: He pursued the emigrating Prophet ﷺ for the bounty, and was told he would one day wear the bracelets of the Persian emperor — which happened in Umar's reign.
A thin sheep too weak to graze gave abundant milk when he ﷺ touched it; her description of him is a classic of the Shamaa'il.

clues: She knelt at a date-drying yard
cards.info: On reaching Madinah he left the choice to his camel, and the masjid was built where she stopped.
On arriving in Madinah he ﷺ paired each emigrant with a helper, binding the two communities into one.
A written agreement setting out rights, duties and common defence among the groups of Madinah.
After about sixteen months facing Bayt al-Maqdis, the direction was turned to the Ka'bah, some of it during a prayer in progress.
He ﷺ sent envoys with letters inviting the rulers of the surrounding empires to Islam.

clues: Tomorrow I shall give the flag
cards.info: The Muslim campaign against the fortified settlements of Khaybar in 7 AH, where Ali (RA) was given the standard.
A poisoned roast was served to him at Khaybar; he ﷺ was warned before eating much, though a companion died from it.
Against the Byzantines in 8 AH; after the three appointed commanders were martyred, Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) saved the army.
An ambush by Hawazin in 8 AH that briefly scattered the Muslims before they regrouped around the Prophet ﷺ.
The difficult march north in 9 AH; the Byzantine force did not appear and the army returned.
The pledge taken under the tree when Uthman (RA) was believed killed; the Qur'an records Allah's pleasure with those who gave it.
The umrah performed the year after Hudaybiyyah, under the terms of that treaty.
After the Conquest, delegations came from across Arabia to accept Islam.

clues: He used to lean on it
cards.info: The trunk he had leaned on while preaching moaned when he moved to a pulpit, until he came down and comforted it.

clues: Everyone drank and filled their vessels
cards.info: Water is reported to have sprung from between his blessed fingers on more than one occasion when the Muslims were thirsty.

cards.word: Feeding the Army at the Trench
clues: A little barley and a young goat
cards.info: Jabir (RA) invited him to a small meal during the digging of the trench; the whole army ate and food remained.
The Muslims helped Salman al-Farsi (RA) meet his master's terms, planting the palms himself ﷺ.
The Islamic calendar was set during Umar's caliphate to begin from the year of the Hijrah.
In his last days he ﷺ directed that Abu Bakr (RA) lead the congregation.
He spent his last days in Aisha's apartment with the permission of his other wives.
Abu Bakr (RA) steadied the community by reciting that Muhammad ﷺ is only a messenger, and messengers pass away.
The Qur'an recounts the believers thrown into a burning trench for refusing to abandon their faith.
The furthest mosque, to which he ﷺ was taken on the night journey and where he led the prophets in prayer.

decks.name: Shamaa'il
decks.subtitle: His noble appearance and ways ﷺ

cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ wore a turban, sometimes with the end hanging between his shoulders; he wore a black turban at the Conquest of Makkah.
The Prophet ﷺ had a slight, beautiful gap between his front teeth, mentioned in descriptions by the companions.
Narrators describe light appearing to emanate from between his front teeth when he ﷺ spoke.
Among his ﷺ described features was a broad, radiant forehead.

cards.word: Hair neither fully straight nor curly
cards.info: His ﷺ hair reached between his earlobes and shoulders, neither fully straight nor tightly curled.
His ﷺ face was slightly rounded with a luminous complexion, likened by companions to the full moon.
He ﷺ had broad shoulders, and between his shoulder blades was the Seal of Prophethood.
His ﷺ palms were full and strong, yet companions said they were softer than silk.
His ﷺ joints and limbs were large and strong, indicating a robust physique.
His ﷺ eyebrows were fine, full and gracefully arched.
His ﷺ eyebrows were full but did not meet in the middle.
A fine vein between his ﷺ eyebrows would become visible when he was angered for the sake of Allah.
His ﷺ neck was described as beautiful like a jug of pure silver in its radiance.
His ﷺ chest and abdomen were in line — his stomach did not protrude beyond his chest.
His ﷺ feet were so smooth that water would run straight off them.
His ﷺ feet had a raised, arched instep.

cards.word: Thin Line of Hair to Navel
cards.info: A fine line of hair ran from his ﷺ chest down to his navel.
A raised mark between his ﷺ shoulder blades, the physical sign of the final Prophet, which Salman al-Farsi sought and saw.
Companions who described him ﷺ concluded they had never seen anyone like him, before or after.
The Prophet ﷺ wore leather socks (khuffain) and permitted wiping over them in wudu.
His ﷺ sandals were of leather with two straps — the famous na'lain sharifain.
His ﷺ pillow was of leather stuffed with palm fibre — a mark of his simple lifestyle.
The Prophet ﷺ loved dates, broke his fast with them, and praised the ajwa dates of Madinah.
He ﷺ would eat cucumber together with fresh dates.
The shoulder was the cut of meat the Prophet ﷺ liked best.
He ﷺ often ate coarse barley bread and sometimes went days without a cooked meal.
He ﷺ said: 'What an excellent condiment vinegar is!' — praising simple, available food.
The Prophet ﷺ loved honey and sweet things, and honey is described in the Qur'an as a healing.
He ﷺ loved milk and taught the du'a asking Allah to bless it and increase it.
He ﷺ used the miswak constantly and said he would have commanded it before every prayer were it not a hardship.
He ﷺ wore a silver ring engraved 'Muhammad Rasulullah', used to seal letters to kings.

cards.word: Walking as if descending a slope
cards.info: He ﷺ walked briskly and purposefully, as if descending a slope.
Companions said the Prophet ﷺ smiled more than anyone they knew.
He ﷺ applied ithmid kohl to his eyes and recommended it, saying it strengthens the sight.

clues: Yet taller than those beside him
cards.info: He ﷺ was of middle stature, though narrators noted he appeared taller than whoever walked with him.
His complexion was luminous and rosy-white, compared by the companions to the full moon.
His eyes were wide and deeply black, with long lashes.
A broad mouth was considered a mark of eloquence among the Arabs, and his ﷺ was described so.
His beard was thick and full; he cared for it and combed it regularly.
Anas (RA) said that the white hairs in his head and beard together did not reach twenty.
Companions described his natural fragrance as finer than musk, lingering wherever he had been.
Umm Sulaym (RA) gathered his perspiration because of its fragrance and blessing.
He ﷺ would lie on his right side, place his hand beneath his cheek, and make du'a before sleeping.
Umar (RA) wept on seeing the impression of the palm-fibre mat pressed into his side.

clues: If he liked it he ate
cards.info: He never found fault with any food: he either ate it or quietly left it alone.
He ﷺ ate using three fingers and would lick them afterwards before wiping his hand.
He drank in three breaths, saying it was more quenching and healthier.
A dish of bread soaked in meat broth, which he ﷺ compared favourably with other foods.
A soothing barley gruel he recommended for the sick and the bereaved.
He ﷺ ate watermelon together with fresh dates, balancing the heat of one with the coolness of the other.
A traditional Arabian dish of dates kneaded with clarified butter and dried curd.

cards.word: Disliked Raw Garlic Before the Masjid
cards.info: He ﷺ asked those who had eaten raw garlic or onion not to come to the mosque until the smell had gone.

clues: His molars would show at most
cards.info: His laughter was mostly a smile; at its fullest his back teeth would just show.

clues: Not a servant, not a woman
cards.info: Aisha (RA) said he never struck anything with his hand except when fighting in the path of Allah.
He would not pull his hand away from a handshake until the other person released it.
When addressing someone he turned his entire body towards them, giving them his full attention.
His gaze was more often downward than upward, in humility and thought.
He made a habit of greeting children when he passed them, and Anas (RA) continued the practice.
A mule presented to him ﷺ, which he rode on several occasions.

clues: Knelt where the masjid was built
cards.info: His well-known camel, associated with the migration and the Farewell Hajj.
A sword that came into his possession at Badr and is famously linked with Ali (RA).
Anas (RA) reported that the garment most beloved to him ﷺ was a striped Yemeni hibarah.

clues: Wear it and shroud your dead in it
cards.info: He ﷺ encouraged wearing white, calling it the best of clothing and the cloth for shrouding.
Among his personal effects; he cared for his hair and parted it.
He kept a container of ithmid and applied it to his eyes, especially at bedtime.

clues: Aisha was asked what he did at home
cards.info: Asked what he did in his house, Aisha (RA) said he mended his sandals, patched his clothes and served his family.
He took part in ordinary household work until it was time for prayer.

clues: Two or three at a time
cards.info: Aisha (RA) described months passing with no cooking fire in their homes, living on dates and water.

clues: I eat as a servant eats
cards.info: He ﷺ refused to eat while leaning back, saying he ate as a servant eats.

cards.word: Never three days of wheat bread
cards.info: His family never had wheat bread three days running until he departed this world.

cards.word: He Did Not Dye His Hair
clues: A point of difference among narrators
cards.info: The stronger reports indicate he did not dye, his grey being too slight to require it.

cards.word: Hair Between the Ears and Shoulders
cards.info: Narrations describe his hair at different times reaching his earlobes, and at others his shoulders.
The ritual prayer, second pillar of Islam, performed five times daily facing the Ka'bah.
Obligatory annual charity of 2.5% on qualifying wealth, given to the poor and other categories — the third pillar.
Abstaining from food, drink and marital relations from dawn to sunset — obligatory in Ramadan, the fourth pillar.
The pilgrimage to Makkah in Dhul Hijjah, obligatory once in a lifetime on those able — the fifth pillar.
The ritual washing of the face, arms, head and feet required before prayer.
The full-body ritual bath required after major impurity, and recommended for Jumu'ah and Eid.
Purification using clean earth when water is unavailable or harmful to use.
The call to prayer announced before each salaah; Bilal (RA) was the first mu'adhin.
The shorter call given immediately before the congregational prayer begins.
The direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah, which Muslims face in prayer; it was changed from Jerusalem in 2 AH.
The bowing position in prayer, glorifying Allah the Magnificent.
Prostration with the forehead on the ground — the position in which a servant is closest to Allah.
The testification recited while sitting in prayer, ending with the declaration of faith.
Turning the head right and left saying 'as-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah' to complete the prayer.
The Friday congregational prayer with its sermon, replacing Dhuhr for men — the weekly Eid of the believers.
The special congregational prayer of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, with additional takbeers.
The extra night prayers of Ramadan performed after Isha, often completing the Qur'an.
The odd-numbered prayer concluding the night's worship, strongly emphasised.
Voluntary charity in any form; the Prophet ﷺ said even a smile is sadaqah.
The minimum amount of wealth (measured in gold or silver) upon which zakaah becomes obligatory.
The pre-dawn meal before fasting; the Prophet ﷺ said there is blessing in it.
The meal breaking the fast at sunset, traditionally begun with dates and water.
Devotional seclusion in the mosque, especially in the last ten days of Ramadan.
The Night of Power in Ramadan, better than a thousand months, on which the Qur'an was sent down.
The sacred state and simple garments assumed for hajj or umrah, with its special restrictions.
Circling the Ka'bah seven times, beginning at the Black Stone.
Walking seven times between Safa and Marwa, commemorating Hajar's search for water.

clues: Without it there is no Hajj
cards.info: The plain where pilgrims stand in supplication on 9 Dhul Hijjah — the essential rite of hajj.
Where pilgrims spend the night after Arafah and gather pebbles for the stoning.
The valley of tents where pilgrims stay during the days of hajj and perform the stoning.
Casting pebbles at three pillars in Mina, recalling Ibrahim's (AS) rejection of shaytan.
The animal sacrifice of Eid al-Adha, commemorating Ibrahim's (AS) willingness to sacrifice his son.
That which Allah has made lawful — in food, earnings and conduct.
That which Allah has prohibited; avoiding it is itself an act of worship.
The Islamic marriage contract, described by the Prophet ﷺ as his sunnah and half of faith.
The obligatory gift from the groom to the bride, which is her exclusive right.
The sacrifice offered on behalf of a newborn, typically on the seventh day, with the head shaved and a name given.
The funeral prayer performed standing with four takbeers — a communal obligation for the deceased.
The declaration that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger — the first pillar of Islam.

clues: In the heart, not the tongue
cards.info: The inward intention that turns an action into worship; the first hadith of Bukhari establishes its weight.
The opening takbeer with which salaah begins and ordinary speech and action become prohibited.
A supplication recited standing in prayer, most commonly in Witr and at times of calamity.
Two prostrations that make up for an error or uncertainty in the prayer.
The prostration made on reciting or hearing one of the verses of prostration in the Qur'an.
Voluntary prayer in the depth of the night, especially in its final third.

clues: After the sun has risen well
cards.info: The forenoon prayer, offered once the sun has risen and before it reaches its zenith.
Two units of prayer followed by a supplication seeking Allah's choice in a matter.
The prayer offered when the sun or moon is eclipsed, distinctive for its repeated ruku.
The prayer seeking rain in time of drought, during which the congregation reverses their cloaks.
The traveller's concession of shortening four-rak'ah prayers to two.
Joining two prayers in one time, permitted on a journey and in certain other circumstances.
Wiping over leather socks in place of washing the feet, for one day and night for a resident and three for a traveller.
The purification of the private parts after answering the call of nature.
Ritual impurity which must be cleaned from the body, garment and place of prayer.
The state following marital relations or seminal discharge, removed by a full bath.
An object placed before one praying alone to mark the limit of their prayer space.
One who joins the congregation after part of it has passed and makes up the rest afterwards.
An act whose performance is required and whose omission is blameworthy.
A binding obligation, distinguished from fard in some schools by the strength of its evidence.
An act that earns reward when performed and carries no blame when left.
An act discouraged in the Sharia without being forbidden outright.
An action that carries no ruling either way in itself.
A payment or feeding made by someone permanently unable to fast.

clues: For a broken oath or fast
cards.info: A prescribed expiation for certain violations, such as breaking an oath or a Ramadan fast deliberately.

clues: For every member of the household
cards.info: The charity given at the end of Ramadan, payable on behalf of each person in the household before the Eid prayer.
Usury or interest, forbidden in the Qur'an in the severest terms.
The dissolution of a marriage, permitted but described as the most detested of lawful things.
The period a woman waits before she may remarry, differing by circumstance.
A relative within a degree that forbids marriage, such as a parent, sibling or child.
The wedding banquet held after the marriage, a confirmed sunnah.
The address delivered before the Friday prayer and on other occasions such as Eid and nikah.
The pilgrim's call of response, recited from entering ihram until the stoning on Eid day.
The final tawaf performed by pilgrims as they depart Makkah.

clues: One of three ways to perform Hajj
cards.info: Performing umrah in the Hajj season, leaving ihram, then entering it again for Hajj.
A single cycle of the prayer, from the standing recitation through to the second prostration.
Ongoing charity whose reward continues after a person dies, named in the hadith of the three lasting deeds.
The performance of an obligatory act after its appointed time has passed.
The prescribed method of slaughter, with the name of Allah pronounced over the animal.

clues: Why you did it, not what you did
cards.info: The opening hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Umar (RA): every deed is judged by the intention behind it, and a man gets only what he intended.
From a long hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari (RA) in Sahih Muslim listing the weight of purification, dhikr and patience.
Tamim ad-Dari (RA) narrated it; when the Companions asked 'To whom?', the Prophet ﷺ answered: to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common folk.

cards.word: Let him speak good or remain silent
cards.info: Part of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (RA): whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or keep silent — and should honour his neighbour and his guest.

cards.word: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself
cards.info: Faith is incomplete while a Muslim wants for himself what he does not want for his brother.

cards.word: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe
cards.info: Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) narrated it; the same hadith defines the emigrant as one who abandons what Allah forbade.

cards.word: The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it
cards.info: Narrated by Uthman ibn Affan (RA) — the standard of excellence tied to learning the Qur'an and passing it on.

cards.word: Make things easy and do not make them difficult
clues: Said to Mu'adh and Abu Musa
cards.info: Instruction to Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) on being sent to Yemen; it continues: give glad tidings and do not drive people away.

cards.word: Allah does not look at your forms and your wealth, but at your hearts and your deeds
cards.info: What is weighed is the state of the heart and the action, not outward form or property.

cards.word: Every act of kindness is charity
cards.info: Narrated by Jabir (RA) — any good turn counts as sadaqah, which opens charity to those with nothing to give.

clues: He asked for advice again and again
cards.info: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for advice and he said 'Do not get angry', repeating it each time the man asked again.

cards.word: The strong man is the one who controls himself when angry
cards.info: The full wording contrasts physical strength with self-mastery: the strong is not the one who overcomes people in wrestling.

cards.word: He who shows no mercy will not be shown mercy
clues: Said when he kissed his grandson
cards.info: Said when a man remarked that he had ten children and had never kissed one of them.

cards.word: The deeds most beloved to Allah are the most constant, even if few
clues: Little and regular beats much and rare
cards.info: Aisha (RA) reported this as the Prophet's ﷺ own habit in worship — steady rather than intense in bursts.

cards.word: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest
cards.info: One of three clauses in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (RA), alongside honouring the neighbour and guarding the tongue.

cards.word: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not harm his neighbour
clues: Same hadith as honouring the guest
cards.info: Jibril (AS) kept urging the Prophet ﷺ about the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would be made an heir.

cards.word: Modesty is a branch of faith
cards.info: From the hadith listing faith's branches — the highest being the declaration of tawhid and the least removing harm from the road.

cards.word: Removing harm from the road is charity
cards.info: Named in the same hadith as the least of faith's branches, and elsewhere as an act of sadaqah in itself.

cards.word: The upper hand is better than the lower hand
clues: Said in a sermon on charity
cards.info: The hand that gives is above the hand that takes; the hadith urges self-sufficiency and restraint from asking.

cards.word: The world is the believer's prison and the disbeliever's paradise
cards.info: However comfortable this life becomes for a believer, it is confinement next to what waits; the reverse for one who denies it.

cards.word: Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise
cards.info: From a long hadith of Abu Hurayrah (RA) on the standing of students and scholars.

cards.word: When a person dies his deeds end except three
clues: A righteous child who prays for him
cards.info: The three are ongoing charity, knowledge benefited from, and a righteous child who supplicates for him.

cards.word: Paradise is surrounded by hardships and the Fire by desires
cards.info: The road to Paradise runs through what the self dislikes; the road to the Fire through what it craves.

cards.word: No one eats better food than what he earns with his own hands
clues: Dawud (AS) ate from his own work
cards.info: The hadith adds that the Prophet of Allah Dawud (AS) used to eat from the work of his own hand.

cards.word: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
clues: A man feared it was pride
cards.info: Said when a man asked whether liking good clothes and shoes was arrogance; the answer was that pride is something else entirely.

cards.word: Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people
clues: Given in the same breath as 'Allah is beautiful'
cards.info: The Prophet's ﷺ own definition, given to distinguish arrogance from simply liking what is good.

cards.word: Whoever deceives us is not one of us
clues: Said at a heap of grain
His hand went inside and found it wet
cards.info: Said after the Prophet ﷺ put his hand into a pile of food for sale and found the lower part damp while the top looked dry.
Listed among the acts of charity available to everyone, whatever their means.

cards.word: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise
clues: Uthman quoted it when rebuilding the Prophet's mosque
cards.info: Uthman (RA) recited this hadith when criticised for rebuilding and expanding the Prophet's mosque.

cards.word: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than praying alone
cards.info: Narrated by Ibn Umar (RA); another authentic narration gives the figure as twenty-five.

cards.word: Whoever prays Fajr is under Allah's protection
cards.info: The hadith warns against falling short in anything that would remove a person from that protection.

cards.word: Ramadan to Ramadan expiates what is between them
clues: As long as major sins are avoided
cards.info: Paired in the same hadith with the five daily prayers and Jumu'ah to Jumu'ah, conditional on avoiding major sins.

cards.word: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward is forgiven
cards.info: The same formula — faith and seeking the reward — is used for standing in prayer during Ramadan and on Laylatul Qadr.

cards.word: Umrah to Umrah is an expiation for what is between them
cards.info: The hadith continues: and an accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise.

cards.word: An accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise
cards.info: A hajj free of sin and accepted by Allah, whose only fitting recompense is Jannah.
One of three things the Prophet ﷺ swore an oath upon, along with forgiveness raising a man's honour and humility raising his rank.
A hadith qudsi: when Allah decreed creation He wrote with Him above the Throne that His mercy prevails over His anger.

cards.word: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole
clues: Learn from it the first time
cards.info: A believer does not let himself be deceived twice by the same trick.

cards.word: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech
clues: Do not spy, do not envy
cards.info: The hadith continues with a chain of prohibitions: do not spy, do not compete in vanity, do not envy, do not hate, and be brothers.

cards.word: Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, be brothers
cards.info: The famous closing of the hadith on suspicion, ending: be servants of Allah, brothers.

cards.word: A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim
clues: He does not wrong him or hand him over
cards.info: The hadith adds that whoever relieves a Muslim's distress will have his own distress relieved on the Day of Judgement.

cards.word: Richness is the richness of the soul
cards.info: Real wealth is not an abundance of goods but a contented heart.

cards.word: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him
cards.info: When Aisha (RA) said that all of them dislike death, he ﷺ explained it refers to the moment the believer is given glad tidings.

cards.word: Be in this world as a stranger or a traveller
clues: Ibn Umar took hold of his shoulders
cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ took Ibn Umar (RA) by the shoulders and said it; Ibn Umar would add: when evening comes do not expect the morning.

cards.word: Whoever calls to guidance has a reward like the rewards of those who follow it
cards.info: Without anything being diminished from their own rewards — and the same applies, in reverse, to calling to error.

cards.word: The best of you is the best to his family
clues: And I am the best of you to my family
cards.info: Graded hasan sahih by at-Tirmidhi. Outside the two Sahihs, so worth verifying before publishing.

clues: Follow a bad deed with a good one
cards.info: Advice to Abu Dharr (RA); it continues: follow a bad deed with a good deed to wipe it out, and treat people with good character. Graded hasan.

cards.word: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt
clues: Hasan and Husayn's grandfather said it to Hasan
cards.info: Narrated by al-Hasan ibn Ali (RA); graded sahih by at-Tirmidhi. Outside the two Sahihs.

cards.word: Part of a person's good Islam is leaving what does not concern him
cards.info: Graded hasan; widely cited as a principle of adab. Outside the two Sahihs.

cards.word: Your smile in the face of your brother is charity
cards.info: Graded hasan by at-Tirmidhi. Outside the two Sahihs, so verify before publishing.

cards.word: Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah
clues: Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi — check grading
cards.info: Graded sahih by at-Tirmidhi. Outside the two Sahihs.

cards.word: All the children of Adam are sinners, and the best of sinners are those who repent
clues: Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah — check grading
cards.info: Graded hasan. Outside the two Sahihs, so worth confirming.
The opening chapter, recited in every unit of prayer — called the Mother of the Book and the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses.
The longest sura (286 verses); shaytan flees a house in which it is recited.
Often called the heart of the Qur'an; widely recited for the sick and the deceased.
Called the best of stories — the account of Yusuf (AS), his brothers, and his rise in Egypt.
The pure declaration of Allah's oneness; reciting it equals a third of the Qur'an in reward.
The two suras of seeking refuge (Falaq and Nas), recited for protection, especially before sleep.
Recited on Fridays; its stories include the sleepers of the cave, and its first verses protect from the Dajjal.
The sura of Dominion, whose nightly recitation intercedes for protection from the punishment of the grave.
Distinguished by its refrain 'Which of your Lord's favours will you both deny?', repeated 31 times.
The greatest verse of the Qur'an (2:255), describing Allah's knowledge and power; recited for protection after each prayer.
Describes the Day of Judgement dividing mankind into three groups; traditionally recited seeking protection from poverty.
The shortest sura, naming the abundance and river granted to the Prophet ﷺ.
The concise sura by which Imam Shafi'i said it would suffice mankind if they pondered it — faith, good deeds, truth and patience.
Recounts Allah's destruction of Abraha's elephant army that marched against the Ka'bah.
Reminds Quraysh of Allah's favour of security and provision through their trade journeys.

clues: Woe to those who pray heedlessly
cards.info: Condemns neglect of the orphan and the needy, and prayer performed for show.
Foretold the Conquest and people entering Islam in crowds — understood as a sign of the Prophet's ﷺ approaching departure.
Condemns Abu Lahab and his wife for their hostility to the Prophet ﷺ.
Describes Laylatul Qadr, on which the Qur'an was sent down and angels descend until dawn.
Describes the final earthquake and that every atom's weight of good or evil will be seen.

clues: Your Lord has not forsaken you
cards.info: Revealed to console the Prophet ﷺ after a pause in revelation: his Lord had not forsaken him.
Named after Maryam (AS); Ja'far (RA) recited it before the Negus of Abyssinia, moving him to tears.
Paradise — the eternal abode of the believers, with eight gates and rewards no eye has seen.
Hellfire — the abode of punishment, from which believers constantly seek Allah's protection.
The bridge over Hellfire that all must cross on the Day of Judgement, traversed according to one's deeds.
The scale on which deeds are weighed on the Day of Judgement.
The Prophet's ﷺ pond, whose drink is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; whoever drinks from it never thirsts again.
'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' — opening every sura but one, and every good action.
One who has memorised the entire Qur'an; their parents will be crowned with light on the Day of Judgement.
The science of reciting the Qur'an correctly and beautifully, as it was revealed.
The thirtieth and final part of the Qur'an, containing the short suras most commonly memorised first.
The Preserved Tablet with Allah, on which all decree is recorded.
The sura whose recitation moved Umar (RA) to Islam; it recounts at length the story of Musa (AS).

clues: A father's advice to his son
cards.info: Named after the wise man whose counsel to his son is preserved in it.

clues: Created you as nations and tribes
cards.info: The sura of social etiquette, containing the verse that the noblest of people are the most God-conscious.
The opening sura of Juz Amma, describing the Day they question one another about.

clues: Glorify the name of your Lord
cards.info: A short Makkan sura frequently recited in the Eid and Friday prayers.
Often recited alongside Sura al-A'laa in the Friday and Eid prayers.
Opens with oaths by the dawn and the ten nights, and ends addressing the tranquil soul.

clues: By the sun and its brightness
cards.info: A short Makkan sura on the purification of the soul and the fate of Thamud.

clues: By the night when it covers
cards.info: Contrasts the one who gives and fears Allah with the one who is miserly and turns away.

clues: Did We not expand your breast
cards.info: A consolation to the Prophet ﷺ, containing the famous promise that with difficulty comes ease.

clues: By the fig and the olive
cards.info: Opens with oaths by the fig, the olive and Mount Sinai, and states that man was created in the finest form.

clues: Read in the name of your Lord
cards.info: The first verses ever revealed, brought to him ﷺ in the Cave of Hira.
The Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) that Allah had commanded him to recite this sura to him.

clues: Man is ungrateful to his Lord
cards.info: Opens with an oath by galloping warhorses before turning to man's ingratitude.
Describes the Day of Judgement and the weighing of deeds.
Warns against being distracted by rivalry in worldly accumulation until death arrives.
Condemns the backbiter and the one obsessed with amassing wealth.
A clear statement of disassociation from disbelief, recommended before sleep.
The verse of debt, the longest in the Qur'an, instructing that loans be written down and witnessed.

clues: Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth
cards.info: The celebrated Verse of Light in Sura an-Nur, describing divine light through an extended image.
The verses at which a prostration is made by the reciter and the listener.

clues: A way of completing the Qur'an weekly
cards.info: A division of the Qur'an into seven parts, and a known selection of verses recited for protection.
One of the thirty equal divisions by which the Qur'an is commonly read.
The classification of revelation by whether it came before or after the migration to Madinah.
The science of explaining the meanings of the Qur'an.
Reciting the Qur'an slowly and clearly, as the Qur'an itself instructs.
The authenticated variant readings of the Qur'an transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ.
The Qur'an in its written, bound form.

clues: Sometimes like the ringing of a bell
cards.info: Divine revelation, which came to the Prophet ﷺ in several described forms.
The Qur'an was revealed in stages across roughly twenty-three years of prophethood.
The formula of seeking refuge in Allah, said before beginning recitation.
The completion of a full reading of the Qur'an, traditionally marked with supplication.

clues: Night and day I called them
cards.info: Recounts Nuh (AS) calling his people over centuries and their persistent refusal.
Contains Isa's (AS) announcement of a messenger to come after him named Ahmad.
Commands believers to leave business for the Friday prayer when the call is made.

clues: Their words differ from their hearts
cards.info: Exposes the hypocrites of Madinah; commonly recited in the second rak'ah of Jumu'ah.

clues: Whoever fears Allah, He makes a way out
cards.info: Sets out the law of divorce and contains the promise of relief and provision for the God-fearing.
Recounts the believers burned in the trench for holding to their faith.
The final Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sent as a mercy to all the worlds.
The Friend of Allah, who built the Ka'bah with his son and was saved when the fire was made cool for him.
The Prophet's ﷺ father, who passed away before his son's birth.
The Prophet's ﷺ mother, who passed away at Abwa when he was about six years old.

clues: The clan is named after him
cards.info: The Prophet's ﷺ great-grandfather, after whom his clan Banu Hashim is named, famed for feeding pilgrims.
The Prophet's ﷺ grandfather, chief of Makkah, who rediscovered the Zamzam well and cared for him after his mother's death.
An ancestor of the Prophet ﷺ in the noble line of Quraysh.
The Prophet's ﷺ uncle who raised and protected him for decades; father of Ali (RA).
The Prophet's ﷺ foster mother from Banu Sa'd, whose household was filled with blessing while she nursed him.
The Prophet's ﷺ first wife and the first person to accept Islam; given glad tidings of a palace in Paradise.
Beloved wife of the Prophet ﷺ and daughter of Abu Bakr, among the greatest scholars and narrators of hadith.
The Prophet's ﷺ beloved daughter, wife of Ali (RA) and mother of Hasan and Husayn, leader of the women of Paradise.
The Prophet's ﷺ grandsons, whom he called the leaders of the youth of Paradise.
The Prophet's ﷺ closest companion, with him in the cave during Hijrah, and the first khalifah.
The second khalifah, famed for justice; the Prophet ﷺ said shaytan takes a different path from Umar's.
The third khalifah, Dhun-Nurayn, who married two of the Prophet's ﷺ daughters and standardised the written Qur'an.
The Prophet's ﷺ cousin and son-in-law, fourth khalifah, who risked his life sleeping in the Prophet's bed on the night of Hijrah.
The Prophet's ﷺ uncle, the Lion of Allah, martyred at Uhud — the leader of the martyrs.
The Abyssinian companion who endured torture proclaiming 'Ahad!' and became the first caller to prayer.
The Persian seeker of truth who found the final Prophet ﷺ and proposed the trench that saved Madinah.
'Father of the kitten' — the companion who narrated more hadith than any other.
The brilliant commander titled the Sword of Allah, undefeated in battle.
The wealthy youth who gave up luxury for Islam and was sent as the first teacher to Madinah before the Hijrah.
The Prophet's ﷺ freed servant who chose to stay with him over his own family — the only companion named in the Qur'an.
Served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years, saying he was never once rebuked with even a word of complaint.
The first human and first prophet, created from clay and taught the names of all things.
The first woman, wife of Adam (AS) and mother of humanity.
The prophet who called his people for 950 years and built the ark before the great flood.
An early prophet described in the Qur'an as truthful and raised to a high station.
Sent to the mighty people of Aad, who were destroyed by a furious wind when they rejected him.
Sent to Thamud with the miraculous she-camel as a sign, which his people fatally hamstrung.
Nephew of Ibrahim (AS), sent to cities steeped in sin which were overturned when they rejected him.
Sent to Madyan, calling them to honesty in weights and measures — known as the orator of the prophets.
The prophet of patience, who endured long illness and loss and was fully restored by Allah.
Swallowed by the whale, he called out in the darkness — 'There is no god but You, glory be to You, I was among the wrongdoers' — and was saved.
Kalimullah — the prophet who spoke with Allah, sent with the staff and other signs to Firawn, and led Bani Isra'il across the sea.
Brother of Musa (AS), granted prophethood as his supporter and spokesman.
Successor of Musa (AS), for whom the sun was held back until victory was achieved.
The prophet-king given the Zabur and a beautiful voice; iron was made soft for him, and he slew Jalut (Goliath).
The prophet-king who commanded the wind and jinn and understood the speech of birds and ants.
Also called Isra'il, father of the twelve tribes, who bore the loss of Yusuf with beautiful patience.
Given half of all beauty; cast into a well by his brothers, he rose to authority in Egypt and forgave them.
Son of Ibrahim (AS), associated with Zamzam and the building of the Ka'bah, and the son of the sacrifice.
Son of Ibrahim (AS) given as glad tidings to Sarah in old age; father of Ya'qub (AS).
Guardian of Maryam (AS), granted the son Yahya in old age after his heartfelt du'a.
Son of Zakariyya (AS), given wisdom in childhood and a name no one had before him.
The Messiah, born miraculously to Maryam (AS), who spoke in the cradle, healed by Allah's permission, and will return before the end of time.
The mother of Isa (AS), chosen above the women of the worlds; the only woman named in the Qur'an, with a sura in her name.
The believing wife of Firawn who rescued the infant Musa (AS) and is among the greatest women of Paradise.
The wise man whose counsel to his son — beginning with avoiding shirk — is preserved in the sura bearing his name.
The righteous ruler who travelled east and west and built the barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj.
The mighty angel of revelation who brought the Qur'an to the Prophet ﷺ.
The angel entrusted with rain and provision, named alongside Jibril in the Qur'an.
The angel who will blow the trumpet announcing the Day of Judgement.
The tyrant of Egypt who claimed divinity, oppressed Bani Isra'il, and was drowned pursuing Musa (AS).
The fiercest Makkan enemy of the Prophet ﷺ, called the Pharaoh of this nation, killed at Badr.
The Prophet's ﷺ uncle and bitter opponent, condemned by name in Sura Masad.
The Abyssinian ruler of Yemen whose elephant army marching on the Ka'bah was destroyed by the birds.
The jinn who refused to prostrate to Adam out of pride and became the avowed enemy of mankind.

clues: Raised the Prophet ﷺ like her own
He gave her his shirt for a shroud
cards.info: Wife of Abu Talib who cared for the orphaned Prophet ﷺ; he honoured her deeply at her death.

clues: He called her 'my mother after my mother'
cards.info: The freed servant who nursed and cared for him ﷺ from childhood and remained devoted all her life.
The Prophet's ﷺ eldest daughter, whose husband later accepted Islam.
Daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and wife of Uthman (RA); she passed away while the Muslims were at Badr.
Her marriage to Uthman (RA) after Ruqayyah's death earned him the title of the possessor of two lights.

clues: The sun eclipsed on the day he died
cards.info: His son who died in infancy; he ﷺ corrected those who linked the eclipse that day to the death.
The first woman he ﷺ married after Khadijah's death.
The compiled pages of the Qur'an were entrusted to her keeping after Abu Bakr's death.
Her counsel at Hudaybiyyah resolved a moment of crisis when the companions hesitated.
She accepted Islam and married the Prophet ﷺ after Khaybar.
The last of the Mothers of the Believers he ﷺ married, during the umrah of 7 AH.

clues: A gift from the ruler of Egypt
cards.info: Sent to the Prophet ﷺ by the Muqawqis of Egypt; mother of his son Ibrahim.
Uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, taken prisoner at Badr before later accepting Islam openly.
Ali's brother, who led the Abyssinian emigrants and was martyred at Mu'tah.

clues: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for his understanding
cards.info: Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the greatest authorities in tafsir.

clues: Among the first to accept Islam
Recited the Qur'an aloud in Makkah
Thin legs, heavy on the scales
cards.info: An early convert renowned for his recitation and knowledge of the Qur'an.

clues: Allah commanded me to recite to you
cards.info: The companion to whom the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to recite Sura al-Bayyinah.
He recorded revelation and later compiled the Qur'an into one volume under Abu Bakr (RA).

clues: Most knowledgeable in halal and haram
I love you, so say this du'a
cards.info: A young companion sent to teach in Yemen, to whom the Prophet ﷺ expressed his love.

clues: The trustworthy one of this nation
cards.info: Given the title of the nation's trustworthy one; a commander in the later conquests.

clues: First to shoot an arrow in Islam
cards.info: Among the earliest Muslims, famed for his accepted du'a and his role at al-Qadisiyyah.
He shielded the Prophet ﷺ with his own body at Uhud, losing the use of his hand.

clues: First to draw a sword for Islam
cards.info: Called the Prophet's ﷺ hawari; among the ten given glad tidings of Paradise.
When offered help on arriving in Madinah he asked only to be shown the marketplace.

clues: Declared Islam aloud in Makkah alone
cards.info: Known for his outspoken truthfulness and severe simplicity of life.

clues: A rebellious party will kill him
cards.info: Among the tortured early Muslims; his parents were the first martyrs of Islam.

clues: Asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for relief
cards.info: An early Muslim whose back bore the scars of torture for his faith.

clues: Bought his freedom with all his wealth
cards.info: He gave up everything he owned to emigrate; the Prophet ﷺ said his trade had profited.

clues: The Throne shook at his death
cards.info: A leader of the Ansar whose death was marked by the trembling of the Throne of the Merciful.

clues: His camel knelt at his door
cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ stayed in his home on arriving in Madinah; he died far away on a campaign.

clues: The poet of the Prophet ﷺ
cards.info: The poet who answered the attacks of Quraysh in verse and was supported in it.
She carried provisions to the cave during the Hijrah, tearing her waistband to fasten the bundle.

clues: Shielded the Prophet ﷺ with her body
cards.info: She defended the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud, taking wounds in doing so.
She accepted Abu Talhah's proposal on condition that he accept Islam, making that her dowry.

clues: The beloved son of the beloved
Commanded an army as a youth
cards.info: Appointed to lead an expedition while still very young, to some people's surprise.
A learned Jewish scholar of Madinah who accepted Islam on meeting the Prophet ﷺ.

clues: Umar was told to seek his du'a
cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ described him to Umar (RA) and instructed that his supplication be sought.

clues: The boat, the boy, the wall
cards.info: The figure in Sura al-Kahf whose actions Musa (AS) could not bear to watch in silence.
Left in the valley of Makkah with her infant son; her search for water is re-enacted in Sa'ee.
Given glad tidings of Ishaq (AS) in her old age.

clues: A hoopoe brought news of her
A throne and a glass floor
cards.info: The queen whose story with Sulaiman (AS) is told in Sura an-Naml.

clues: Tested his army at a river
cards.info: The king appointed over Bani Isra'il who tested his soldiers at the river before facing Jalut.
The tyrant defeated by the young Dawud (AS).
A man of Musa's (AS) people whose wealth made him arrogant until the earth swallowed him and his house.
The associate of Firawn who was ordered to build a lofty tower.
The one who fashioned the calf that Bani Isra'il worshipped in Musa's (AS) absence.
The young believers who took refuge in a cave and slept for centuries, recounted in Sura al-Kahf.
Mentioned twice in the Qur'an among the patient and the righteous.
A prophet of Bani Isra'il named among the excellent in the Qur'an.
A prophet who called his people away from the worship of Ba'l.
Caused to die for a century and then revived, with his food unspoiled and his donkey restored before his eyes.
The house of Allah in Makkah that Muslims all over the world face when they pray.
The mosque — the place where Muslims gather for prayer.
The washing done before prayer: face, arms to the elbows, wiping the head, and the feet.
The call that tells everyone it is time to pray.
The mat Muslims pray on, laid facing the direction of the Ka'bah.
Putting the forehead on the ground in prayer — the position closest to Allah.

clues: The Qur'an came down in it
cards.info: The month in which Muslims fast from dawn until sunset.
The meal that breaks the fast at sunset, usually begun with dates and water.
The meal eaten before dawn by someone who is going to fast.
The two celebrations of the Muslim year, after Ramadan and at the time of Hajj.
The fruit the Prophet ﷺ loved and broke his fast with.

clues: A baby's heel made it come
cards.info: The well that sprang up in the desert for baby Isma'il (AS) and his mother, still flowing today.

clues: What you say when you arrive
cards.info: The Muslim greeting of peace, which should always be returned.
Said at the beginning of anything good — eating, drinking, starting work.
Praise and thanks to Allah, said after eating and at every blessing.
The book Allah revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, treated with the greatest respect.
Supplication — speaking to Allah and asking Him for what you need.
Counting the praises of Allah, often on a string of beads.
The natural toothbrush the Prophet ﷺ used and encouraged.
The one who leads the congregation in prayer.
The Friday prayer, when Muslims gather together to listen and pray.
Creatures made of light who carry out Allah's commands and never disobey.
Paradise — the beautiful home Allah has promised to those who believe and do good.
The enemy who tries to make people forget Allah; we seek refuge from him.
The boat Nuh (AS) built, which carried the believers and the animals through the great flood.
Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a great fish and called on Allah in the darkness until he was saved.
When Ibrahim (AS) was thrown into the fire, Allah commanded it to be cool and safe for him.
The staff of Musa (AS), which became a serpent and parted the sea for his people.
Sulaiman (AS) understood the ant who warned her colony to move before the army arrived.
The bird that brought Sulaiman (AS) news of the Queen of Sheba.
The miraculous she-camel given to the people of Thamud as a sign, which they killed.
A spider's web at the mouth of the cave helped conceal the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) during the Hijrah.
The cave where the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) sheltered on their way to Madinah.

clues: They came to break the Ka'bah
cards.info: The army that marched on the Ka'bah with elephants and was destroyed by flocks of birds.
Maryam (AS) was told to shake the palm trunk so ripe dates would fall for her.
Yusuf (AS) dreamed that eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowed to him.
Yusuf's (AS) brothers threw him into a well, where a passing caravan found him.
Hajar ran between Safa and Marwa looking for water for her baby, and Zamzam appeared.
The five prayers every Muslim performs each day.
The dawn prayer, offered before sunrise.
The prayer at sunset.

clues: There is an arrow in hotel rooms
cards.info: The direction of the Ka'bah, which Muslims face in prayer.
Charity — anything given to help another person.
Truthfulness, one of the qualities the Prophet ﷺ was known for even before prophethood.

clues: A woman was forgiven for it
cards.info: A woman was forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog; Islam teaches mercy to every creature.

clues: Say it with your mum and dad
cards.info: Honouring parents is commanded in the Qur'an right after worshipping Allah alone.
Giving others a share of what you have, which the Prophet ﷺ practised all his life.
The Prophet ﷺ said smiling at your brother is charity.
Admitting a mistake and asking forgiveness, from Allah and from people.

clues: A thin curve in the sky
We look for it before Ramadan
cards.info: The new moon that marks the start of each Islamic month.
The tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.
Shoes are removed before entering the prayer area to keep it clean.

clues: The Prophet ﷺ liked it for good things
cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ used his right hand for eating, drinking and all good things.
A cap worn on the head, often for prayer.
The great pilgrimage to Makkah that every able Muslim makes once if they can.
Walking seven times around the Ka'bah.
The sacrifice made at Eid al-Adha, with the meat shared with family, neighbours and the poor.

clues: The first to call the adhan
He was a slave and was freed
cards.info: The companion who became the first caller to prayer in Islam.
The final Messenger of Allah, sent as a mercy to all the worlds.
A wife of the Prophet ﷺ who became one of the greatest teachers of Islam.
The beloved daughter of the Prophet ﷺ.
Cleanliness before eating is part of the manners the Prophet ﷺ taught.
The way the Prophet ﷺ lay down to sleep.
The prayer offered after the sun passes its highest point.
The night prayer, the last of the five.

clues: Hands go up to your ears
cards.info: Saying Allahu Akbar, with which the prayer begins.
Said at the end of Surah al-Fatihah in prayer.
The opening chapter of the Qur'an, recited in every unit of prayer.

clues: Worth a third of the Qur'an
cards.info: The short surah about Allah being One, whose reward equals a third of the Qur'an.
The Verse of the Throne, recited for protection after prayers and before sleep.

clues: The teacher is called apa or moulana
cards.info: The class where Muslim children learn to read the Qur'an and about their religion.
The extra night prayers performed during Ramadan.
The gift of money children traditionally receive at Eid.
Wearing your best and clean clothes on the day of Eid.
The embrace and greeting exchanged after the Eid prayer.

clues: In the corner of the Ka'bah
cards.info: The stone set into the corner of the Ka'bah that pilgrims greet as they pass.
The two hills pilgrims walk between, remembering Hajar's search for water.
The simple white garments worn for Hajj and Umrah.

clues: It can go days without water
cards.info: The animal of the desert, mentioned in the Qur'an as a sign for people to reflect on.

clues: The Qur'an has a surah about them
cards.info: Allah taught the bee to make honey, which the Qur'an describes as a healing.
The ant that warned her colony when Sulaiman's (AS) army approached.
The Prophet ﷺ was kind to cats, and Abu Hurairah was named for the kitten he carried.
Musa (AS) was placed in a basket on the river as a baby and found by Firawn's household.
Musa (AS) struck the sea with his staff and it opened a path for his people.
Ibrahim (AS) broke the idols of his people and told them to ask the largest one what happened.

clues: It came instead of his son
cards.info: Allah sent a ram in place of Ibrahim's (AS) son, remembered every Eid al-Adha.
Isa (AS) spoke while still an infant to defend Maryam (AS).
Dawud (AS) had so beautiful a voice that the mountains and birds praised Allah with him.

clues: He was ill a long time
cards.info: Ayyub (AS) endured long illness and loss without losing patience.

clues: Do not eat from that tree
cards.info: Adam (AS), the first human, who repented after his mistake and was forgiven.
The beautiful names of Allah, describing His mercy, power and kindness.
A declaration that Allah is greater than everything.
Said in wonder at Allah's creation and in remembrance after prayer.

clues: Say it about your friend's new bike
cards.info: Said to show appreciation for a blessing, without envy.
Said about anything in the future, because nothing happens except by Allah's will.
A way of thanking someone by asking Allah to reward them.
Seeking Allah's forgiveness.
The first month of the Islamic calendar.
The month in which the Prophet ﷺ was born.
The month of the pilgrimage and of Eid al-Adha.
Visiting someone who is unwell, which the Prophet ﷺ strongly encouraged.
Neighbours have great rights in Islam, whoever they are.

clues: Like two fingers together in Jannah
cards.info: The Prophet ﷺ promised closeness in Paradise to whoever cares for an orphan.
Feeding the hungry is among the deeds most praised in the Qur'an and Sunnah.
Truthfulness is a central quality of a Muslim.
